metadata.section: MAINTENANCE OF VARIATION BY DIRECT SELECTION
subsections: MAINTENANCE OF VARIATION BY DIRECT SELECTION
metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: As shown in Figure 28.1, a number of models for the maintenance of variation assume stabilizing selection on the focal trait. We start by examining stabilizing selection per se on both one, and n, traits. The conclusion is that only very limited amounts of genetic variation can be maintained in such settings, especially if a large number of genes, each of modest to small effect, underlie the trait. One potential countering selective force will arise if trait loci have overdominant pleiotropic effects on fitness, and this is discussed next. Such overdominance can arise when homozygotes have a higher environmental variance than heterozygotes for a trait under strict stabilizing selection. Fitness overdominance can also be generated when the underlying loci show $ G E $ in the trait under selection, and we will examine both of these situations. Finally, the impacts of a changing optimum phenotypic value and frequency-dependent selection will be examined to see if these can help retain variation. As we detail, all of these models fall short in their attempt to account for observed levels of variation.
